advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the SNAPSHOT keyring migration reseed genesis records with the CREATE event's full `{timestamp}-{uuid}` position, not the bare `created_at` timestamp.
evidence: `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring(state, str(state.get("created_at") or ""))` — migration call passes `created_at`
src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:150: `state["created_at"] = event.get("timestamp")` — created_at is the timestamp ONLY, no uuid
src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:198: `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring(state, f"{event.get('timestamp')}-{event.get('uuid')}")` — the fresh CREATE path uses the full `{timestamp}-{uuid}` position

authorship.py resolve_event_commit globs `f"{rel}/{position}-*.json"` (authorship.py:148); with a bare-timestamp position this becomes `<timestamp>-*.json`, matching any event sharing that timestamp and returning `lines[-1]` — potentially the wrong add-commit
advisory.finding: The SNAPSHOT-restore keyring migration reseeds genesis records with a bare timestamp instead of a full `{timestamp}-{uuid}` position, so a migrated genesis key's `added_at` will not resolve to a unique introducing commit.
advisory.suggested_fix: Persist the CREATE position (timestamp+uuid) into compiled state (e.g. store a `create_position` on the identity) and pass that to `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring` in the migration branch, rather than `created_at`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Compare intra-commit positions by integer timestamp prefix (matching reducer._sort), not lexicographic string comparison.
evidence: authorship.py:219: `added = added_at <= event_position` (string comparison of `{timestamp}-{uuid}`)
authorship.py:230-231: `revoked = revoked_at <= event_position` (same string comparison)
src/rebar/reducer/_sort.py:20-25: `prefix_ts` compares the timestamp prefix as an INTEGER
src/rebar/reducer/_sort.py:5-6: docstring — 'integer comparison orders them ... regardless of digit width — string comparison only agrees while every name has the same width'
advisory.finding: verify_authorship_at_commit's intra-commit refinement compares positions with lexicographic string `<=`, which disagrees with the canonical integer-prefix replay ordering when event timestamps within a commit differ in digit width.
advisory.suggested_fix: Split each position into (int(timestamp), uuid) and compare tuples, reusing `reducer._sort.prefix_ts` semantics so the refinement matches replay order exactly.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the revoke-commit resolution in verify_authorship_at_commit fail CLOSED: when revoked_at is a non-empty position but resolve_event_commit returns None, treat the key as revoked (drop it) rather than valid, matching the add-path fail-closed behavior.
evidence: Add path fails closed: `added_commit = resolve_event_commit(added_at, ...)` then `if added_commit is None:` `continue` (authorship.py:214-216)

Revoke path fails open: `revoked = False` ... `revoked_commit = resolve_event_commit(revoked_at, ...)` `if revoked_commit is not None:` (only then is ancestry checked); a None revoked_commit leaves `revoked=False` so the key is appended to `valid_keys` (authorship.py:225-235)
resolve_event_commit returns None on `proc.returncode != 0`, empty output, or any exception (authorship.py:155-160) — all of which are reachable for a stored revoke position

A key whose add resolves but whose revoke does not is emitted into `trust_root = allowed_signers_from_keys(valid_keys, ...)` (authorship.py:254), so a revoked key verifies as author — the same class of backdating/rewind bypass this change set out to close
advisory.finding: verify_authorship_at_commit fails OPEN on the revocation check: if a key's revoked_at position cannot be resolved to a commit (resolve_event_commit returns None on git failure, glob miss, or history rewrite), the `if revoked_commit is not None:` guard is skipped, `revoked` stays False, and the revoked key is added to the trust root — resurrecting a revoked key's authorship authority. The add-commit path fails CLOSED (added_commit is None -> continue) but the revoke path does not.
scenarios: A KEY_REVOKE event file's introducing commit becomes unresolvable (glob miss after a merge/history rewrite, transient git error, or timeout) while the KEY_ADD still resolves
An attacker who can perturb git-log resolution of the revoke position (but not the add) restores a revoked key's ability to author events
advisory.suggested_fix: In the revoke branch, when `revoked_at` is a non-empty string, treat an unresolvable revoke commit as revoked: e.g. `if isinstance(revoked_at, str) and revoked_at:` then `revoked_commit = resolve_event_commit(...)`; `if revoked_commit is None: revoked = True` (fail closed) else apply the ancestry/position logic.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify resolve_event_commit's multi-match handling: choosing lines[-1] (oldest add) for added_at widens validity; confirm the position glob cannot match multiple distinct events/commits, or select the resolution direction that fails closed per use.
evidence: `lines = [ln.strip() for ln in proc.stdout.splitlines() if ln.strip()]` then `return lines[-1] if lines else None` (authorship.py:157-158)
The glob is prefix-only and type-agnostic: `pathspec = f"{rel}/{position}-*.json"` (authorship.py:148) — a position prefix collision across commits yields multiple add commits
Downstream ancestry decides validity from this single returned commit (authorship.py:214, 221, 227-232)
advisory.finding: resolve_event_commit returns lines[-1] (the oldest 'A' commit) when a position prefix matches an event added in more than one commit. For the added_at side this selects the earliest add, widening a key's validity window earlier than its true introduction; the revoke side has no symmetric hardening, so a multi-match interacts with the fail-open revocation branch to further favor treating keys as valid.
scenarios: An event file matching the position glob is re-materialized/re-added across commits (merge conflict resolution, snapshot round-trip, or a colliding prefix), producing multiple `--diff-filter=A` commits

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace test_hlc_epoch_surface_absent's source-grep with a behavioral assertion (e.g. assert the removed functions are not importable/callable and that produced keyring records contain no epoch fields) rather than grepping implementation text.
evidence: for path in root.rglob("*.py"): text = path.read_text(...) ... if sym in text: hits.append(...)
banned_functions = ["verify_authorship_at_epoch", "epoch_for_position", "keys_valid_at_epoch"]

This greps executable source under test (not a non-executable instruction artifact), so the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception does not apply; the assertion is on implementation text, satisfying the refactoring-violation defect criterion.
advisory.finding: test_hlc_epoch_surface_absent (AC7) greps the SOURCE UNDER TEST (all `*.py` under the rebar package, including authorship.py and reducer/_processors.py) for banned function-name and dict-key string literals, asserting on the text of the implementation rather than its behavior. It is a source-grepping change-detector: it breaks on a behavior-preserving rename and would misfire on an unrelated symbol/string collision, while a functional regression that still avoids those exact tokens would pass.
scenarios: A private helper is renamed to a name colliding with a banned token, or an epoch symbol is reintroduced under a new name — test gives a false pass/fail without any behavior change.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert `not hasattr(authorship, 'verify_authorship_at_epoch')` etc. and inspect a produced keyring record's keys for absent `added_epoch`/`revoked_epoch`, instead of scanning `*.py` text.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Enforce reducer purity behaviorally (e.g. monkeypatch subprocess.run/os to raise during a replay and assert reduction still succeeds) rather than grepping reducer source text.
evidence: for path in reducer_dir.rglob("*.py"): text = path.read_text(...) ; if "import subprocess" in text or "merge-base" in text or "--diff-filter" in text: offenders.append(...)
The grep targets SOURCE CODE UNDER TEST, not an instruction artifact, so this is source-grepping (refactoring-violation criterion), not a Rule-5 structural-boundary assertion.
advisory.finding: test_reducer_stays_pure (AC8) greps reducer source files for the strings 'import subprocess', 'merge-base', and '--diff-filter'. This asserts on implementation text of the code under test, so it is a change-detector: a mere comment mentioning 'merge-base' trips it, and a reducer that performs git I/O via a different mechanism (e.g. os.system or an indirect import) passes — the invariant it claims to protect (reducer purity) is not actually enforced by observable behavior.
scenarios: A reducer file adds a docstring/comment referencing 'merge-base' (false failure); or introduces git side-effects via os.system / a helper import (false pass).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that compacts KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE into a SNAPSHOT (and/or restores a stale epoch-era keyring) and asserts the position-based keyring is re-seeded and keyring_epoch is dropped.
evidence: _processors.py:778-784: `_restored_ring = state.get("keyring") or []` ... `if "keyring" not in compiled_state or _stale_epoch_era: state.pop("keyring_epoch", None); _bootstrap_genesis_keyring(...)`
Both fixtures: `monkeypatch.setenv("REBAR_COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS", "9" * 18)` with comment `# keep events unfolded` (test_identity_ts2_09f9.py:32, heldout:...)
ABSENCE: search for 'SNAPSHOT' in test_identity_ts2_09f9_heldout.py returns no matches; no test restores a stale/epoch-era or keyring-less snapshot.
advisory.finding: The process_snapshot keyring migration branch (SCHEMA_VERSION 5: drop stale keyring_epoch and re-seed a genesis keyring from static keys when a snapshot lacks keyring or carries epoch-era records) has no test. Both test fixtures set REBAR_COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS='9'*18 to keep events UNFOLDED, so no SNAPSHOT is ever produced or restored, leaving the migration code path entirely unexercised.
scenarios: Compaction squashes KEY events into a SNAPSHOT, or a pre-v6 clone's epoch-era snapshot is restored: a regression in the migration (failing to drop keyring_epoch, or mis-seeding) silently corrupts the trust root.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that supplies a valid signature over a different op/identity/public_key and asserts add/revoke is refused (payload-mismatch).
evidence: identity.py:228-232: `if signature.payload != expected: raise CommandError(... payload mismatch ...)`

ABSENCE: search for 'payload_mismatch' in tests/unit returns no matches; heldout AC2 (test_unsigned_non_genesis_key_add_refused) passes signature=None, exercising only the isinstance guard at line 223, not the payload check.
advisory.finding: The payload-mismatch replay-refusal check in _verify_keyop_signature (step 1: reject a signature whose payload is not exactly keyop_payload(op, identity_id, public_key)) is untested. AC2 only covers the missing-signature refusal; a valid signature over a DIFFERENT op/identity/key being replayed to authorize this operation — the specific replay attack this branch exists to stop — is never exercised.
scenarios: An attacker replays a validly-signed KEY_REVOKE envelope (correct signer, wrong key/identity) to authorize a KEY_ADD — must be refused by the payload check.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a reducer test asserting a KEY_REVOKE for an unknown/already-revoked key leaves keyring and derived keys unchanged.
evidence: _processors.py KEY_REVOKE branch: iterates keyring for first matching record with `revoked_at is None`, `break`; docstring: 'a revoke naming an unknown / already-revoked key folds no change'
ABSENCE: only AC1/AC3 revoke a currently-valid key; no test folds a KEY_REVOKE for an absent or twice-revoked key.
advisory.finding: The KEY_REVOKE-of-unknown / already-revoked key fold-no-change branch in process_key_event is untested. The processor documents that a revoke naming an unknown or already-revoked key folds no change, but no test asserts the keyring/keys are unchanged in that case.
scenarios: A KEY_REVOKE arrives (via forward-compat/out-of-order replay) for a key not in the ring or already revoked; a regression could revoke the wrong record or mutate state.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the snapshot-restore keyring migration seed `added_at` with the full `{timestamp}-{uuid}` CREATE position (not the bare `created_at` timestamp) so it matches the process_create bootstrap and resolves to the CREATE commit.
evidence: process_create seeds with the FULL position: `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring(state, f"{event.get('timestamp')}-{event.get('uuid')}")` (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:198)
the snapshot migration seeds with only the timestamp: `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring(state, str(state.get("created_at") or ""))` (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:784)
`created_at` is set to the timestamp WITHOUT the uuid: `state["created_at"] = event.get("timestamp")` (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:150)

event filenames are `{timestamp}-{uuid}-{TYPE}.json` (src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:109) and the resolver globs `pathspec = f"{rel}/{position}-*.json"` (src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:148), so a bare-timestamp `added_at` produces `{timestamp}-*.json` which is not the canonical position prefix and may match a different event / resolve to the wrong introducing commit

the migration comment claims parity — 'every key added at the CREATE position' (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:775) and _bootstrap_genesis_keyring docstring says added_at is 'the CREATE event's {timestamp}-{uuid} prefix' (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:88-89) — but the value passed at line 784 is not that prefix
migration branch: `if "keyring" not in compiled_state or _stale_epoch_era:` then `state.pop("keyring_epoch", None); _bootstrap_genesis_keyring(state, ...)` (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:782-784)

_bootstrap_genesis_keyring returns without seeding when keys is empty/absent: `if state.get("ticket_type") != "identity" or not isinstance(keys, list) or not keys: return` (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:94)
the migration explicitly discards the stale epoch keyring records (`do NOT trust the stale fields`) and relies solely on the static `keys` re-seed (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:773-776)
ABSENCE: the epoch-era snapshot's compiled_state shape is not in this diff, so whether it always carries `keys` alongside the epoch keyring cannot be confirmed from the changed files
advisory.finding: Snapshot-restore keyring migration seeds genesis records with a bare timestamp as `added_at`, not the canonical `{timestamp}-{uuid}` position the live CREATE path uses — an asymmetric replace that yields inconsistent keyring records and a mis-resolving commit anchor.
merged_from: The snapshot-restore keyring migration re-seeds exclusively from `state.get('keys')`; if a stale epoch-era snapshot's compiled_state does not carry a static `keys` list, the migration silently produces an empty keyring, dropping the identity's keys.
scenarios: An identity whose events were compacted into a SNAPSHOT before this feature (or an epoch-era snapshot) is replayed: its genesis keyring records get `added_at=<bare timestamp>` while an un-compacted clone of the same identity gets `added_at=<timestamp-uuid>`; the two states diverge.

verify_authorship_at_commit calls resolve_event_commit on the bare-timestamp `added_at`; the glob fails to match uniquely (or matches an unrelated same-timestamp event) so the add-commit resolves wrong or to None, dropping the key from the trust root.
advisory.suggested_fix: Persist and use the full CREATE position for the restore path — e.g. project a `created_position` (`{timestamp}-{uuid}`) onto state at CREATE and pass that to `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring` in process_snapshot, instead of `state.get('created_at')`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update docs/api-stability.md and docs/event-schema.md to reflect SCHEMA_VERSION=5 (and note the v4/v5 keyring changes) so the documented event-schema contract matches reducer/_version.py.

Not a runtime break (the bump is declarative preserve-and-ignore and nothing gates on the integer; ticket_state schema is additionalProperties:true), but the documented event-schema contract drifts from code.
advisory.suggested_fix: In docs/api-stability.md:24 and docs/event-schema.md:74 change 'currently 3' to 5 and add the v4 (KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE body types) and v5 (position-based keyring projection) entries mirroring the _version.py changelog.
